newsitem.title: USA: U.S. insists OSCE will run Bosnia local elections.
newsitem.headline: U.S. insists OSCE will run Bosnia local elections.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday accused Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic of blocking elections in Bosnia and said the Serbs should understand "right now" that international officials will run a local vote next year.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns was speaking after U.S. envoy John Kornblum failed to get Plavsic to agree that planned municipal elections should be supervised by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
"Unfortunately, I have to report to you that Mrs. Plavsic remains an impediment to the electoral process," Burns told a news briefing.

"The United States in response to that is going to maintain a very heavy active diplomatic involvement and presence to make sure that in the end the OSCE supervises and monitors those elections," he said.
"That will be the result here, and the Bosnian Serbs ought to understand that right now."

Kornblum said in Sarajevo that the only way to achieve confidence in the elections was to extend the mandate of the OSCE, which supervised general elections in Bosnia on Sept. 14. But he said he had failed to persuade Plavsic to endorse this.
OSCE officials said, however, they believed Plavsic had not closed the door on OSCE supervision.
The OSCE announced on Tuesday the elections had been postponed from November to an unspecified date next year.

Bosnia's Moslems and Croats have agreed to OSCE supervision, but the Serbs have criticised voter registration rules set down by the OSCE that aim to prevent nationalist authorities from concentrating votes in disputed towns.
They fear Moslem refugees will vote them out of power in municipalities where Moslem majorities were expelled during the 43-month war in Bosnia.
